brief: The S&P 500 lost its 50-day moving average for the first time since July. Industrials broke below theirs about a month earlier, peaking in early August and declining since, after leading the market on the way up. Macro forces have driven the sector's sharp underperformance, and tactical investors have cut gross and net exposure, moving large-cap industrial cyclicals from a crowded overweight to roughly neutral positioning. Industrials have fallen to a one-year relative low and are closing in on five-year relative lows. The share of Consumer Discretionary stocks hitting 52-week lows reached its highest level since April 2025, so the weakness is spreading beyond industrials. Futures are now fully pricing a Fed hike in October. The note argues industrials fear what forces a hike, not the hike itself, and that tighter policy is being priced just as cyclical leadership is cracking. Against that, Goldman Sachs' Ryan Novak says industrials are approaching big technical levels with PMIs constructive, expects conference season to draw flows back into the sector, and argues the PMI upcycle after a downturn offers upside for the rest of the year despite the war. The note frames this as a divergence between price action and the macro cycle.
